messages.content: You design amateur rockets that fly on certified commercial motors. Work through the design, check it with the tools, and give the final design as JSON inside <design> tags. Only report results the tools returned.
Requirement: Need around 475 m apogee. It should fit an 18 mm motor case. Only standard Estes-size motors, D or smaller. Our field sits about 1,300 m above sea level.

messages.reasoning_content:
1. Understand: apogee about 475 m (approximate, within 5%). The motor case is 18 mm (fixed). Motors are standard Estes, class D or smaller (maximum). The field is about 1,300 m above sea level (approximate site altitude). Wind, rail, landing speed and launch angle are not stated, so I assume 2 m/s, a 1.5 m rail, a 6 m/s landing and a vertical launch. Single stage.
2. Feasibility: no-drag speed for 475 m is sqrt(2*9.81*475) = 97 m/s. Thin air at 1,300 m helps, but an 18 mm Estes case rules out the usual 24 mm D12. A C in a slim tube is the realistic choice, and it has to be checked against the band rather than assumed. Looking up the Estes candidates that might fit.

2. Feasibility: the D12 is Estes and class D, but the case is 0.024 m, so it does not fit an 18 mm mount. Estes D16 is not in the database. The C6 is Estes, class C, 8.8 N*s, 4.8 N average, an 18 mm case (0.018 m by 0.07 m, 0.0231 kg) with 0, 3, 5 and 7 s delays. The C5 is also 18 mm but only 7.8 N*s and a single 3 s delay. The C6 is the one that can reach the mid-400s in thin air. I will use the 5 s delay.
3. Size: guessed liftoff mass 0.045 kg. Thrust-to-weight = 4.8 / (0.045 * 9.81) = 10.9. Pad weight 0.045 * 9.81 = 0.442 N, rail acceleration (4.8 - 0.442) / 0.045 = 96.8 m/s^2, exit speed sqrt(2 * 96.8 * 1.5) = 17.0 m/s on the average thrust. The C6 spike should push the real exit higher. Propellant is 0.011 kg, descent mass 0.045 - 0.011 = 0.034 kg. Chute for 5 m/s: area 2 * 0.034 * 9.81 / (1.225 * 0.8 * 5^2) = 0.0272 m^2, diameter sqrt(4 * 0.0272 / 3.1416) = 0.186 m. I will use a 0.30 m chute. The 1,300 m site is passed as the site altitude; wind and rail stay at the defaults.
4. Draft: 0.10 m ogive polystyrene nose on a 0.36 m cardboard tube, outer diameter 0.022 m, wall 0.4 mm. Mount 0.019 m outside, 0.07 m long, Estes C6 with a 5 s delay. Three balsa fins, root 0.055 m, tip 0.022 m, span 0.038 m, sweep 0.025 m, 1.6 mm thick. Chute 0.30 m polyethylene on ejection. Site altitude 1,300 m.

4. Check: the thin air was not enough. The simulator gives 420.3 m, and (475 - 420.3) / 475 = 12% under about 475 m. The 5% band starts near 451 m, so 475 - 420.3 = 54.7 m is still short. Everything else passes: rail exit 28.4 m/s, thrust-to-weight 11.8, margin 2.21 cal, landing 3.1 m/s. The C6 is an 18 mm Estes motor, class C. The chute opens at 6.9 s, just before the 7.21 s apogee. Mass is 0.0415 kg. Site altitude in the run is 1,300 m.
5. Fix: the failing value is 420.3 m. Margin is 2.21 cal, so the fins are larger than they need to be, and the 0.36 m tube is more skin than a C6 needs. I am cutting drag in both places: tube length 0.36 m to 0.28 m, and fins to root 0.045 m, tip 0.018 m, span 0.030 m, sweep 0.020 m. Motor, nose and chute stay. That should pick up the missing 55 m without dropping the margin under 1 cal.

4. Check: the shorter tube and smaller fins landed in the band. The simulator gives 461.9 m, and (475 - 461.9) / 475 = 2.8% low, inside 5%. 475 - 461.9 = 13.1 m. Rail exit 28.3 m/s, thrust-to-weight 12.4, margin 1.1 cal at the rail and through the burn, landing 3.0 m/s. The motor is an Estes C6, 18 mm, class C. The chute opens at 6.9 s, just before the 7.23 s apogee. Site altitude is 1,300 m. Mass is 0.0396 kg.
5. Fix: no further change. Altitude, motor case, motor class and the safety gates all pass.
6. Uncertainty: 1.1 cal is close to the 1.0 cal floor, and 461.9 m is on the low side of the band. A slightly heavy build, or fins sanded even smaller, can miss one or the other. The 1,300 m site is doing real work; the same rocket at sea level would come back near the first draft's 420 m. Chute Cd and the real cardboard mass will move both the landing rate and the apogee.
messages.content:
Estes C6-5 in a short 22 mm cardboard rocket, flown from a 1,300 m site. The case is 18 mm and the class is C.
Apogee is 461.9 m, about 3% under 475 m. It leaves a 1.5 m rail at 28.3 m/s and lands at 3.0 m/s under a 0.30 m chute.
Margin is 1.1 cal, just over the 1 cal floor.
